primary_claim: In LoRA adapters fine-tuned on Llama 3.2-3B and 3.1-8B at various 'doses' of bad medical advice, layer-12 residual-stream activation cosine drift toward the fully-poisoned model reaches 28% of full-poisoning drift at just 5% dose, while behavioral (LLM-judge) misalignment detection shows essentially no signal until 50%+ dose, revealing a substantial detection gap between activation-based and behavioral emergent-misalignment audits.

effect.metric: activation cosine drift toward fully-poisoned model, at 5% poisoning dose
effect.value: 28% of full-poisoning drift level at 5% dose vs. no behavioral signal until 50%+ dose

contradicts_or_qualifies: Extends Betley et al. 2025b and Turner et al. 2025's emergent misalignment findings by showing behavioral detection substantially underestimates misalignment risk at low poisoning doses relative to activation-level drift

At 8B scale, Betley et al. 2025b's Deception eval still outperforms the author's autoresearch-optimized prompt set, qualifying the value of prompt optimization relative to the original Deception battery
stated_future_work: Explore whether behavioral detection could be improved by fine-tuning misalignment judges (judge distillation from activation-drift/probe targets)
Explore judge distillation further in a planned follow-on post
limitations_stated: Explicitly labeled an exploration with a bare-bones compute budget; conclusions are exploratory
Replication on other models and bad-data types would strengthen the conclusions
Optimized prompt sets, while improving on the EM papers' original questions, still don't match the discriminative power of Betley et al. 2025b's own Deception battery for larger models
quote: Even at 5% dosage levels, model activation directions drift 28% of the way toward those in 100% adapters.
